headline: Sterling has slipped to about 1.3219 against the dollar by 12:40 Dubai on Thursday, from 1.3263 at Wednesday's close, as the dollar strengthened across the board with US 10-year and 30-year yields at new highs and the euro below $1.13 for the first time since May 2025. Governor Bailey's opening remarks at a Bank of England conference on the future of money carried no news on interest rates in the reports read, and the pound kept drifting lower after them.

happened.event: Bank of England Governor Bailey opens the Future of Money conference
happened.result: Bailey gave opening remarks at a conference on digital money held in honour of the economist Charles Goodhart. The morning briefings read carried his warning that the AI boom could trigger market shocks, and nothing on the path of Bank Rate.
happened.why: Only remarks pointing to higher or lower UK interest rates tend to move the pound much, so a speech without them leaves sterling to follow the dollar.
happened.effect: GBP/USD was about 1.3232 just before he spoke and moved between 1.3227 and 1.3236 in the first five minutes. It then drifted down to about 1.3219 by 08:38 UTC (12:38 Dubai) as the dollar stayed firm.

happened.event: Dollar buying at the London open
happened.result: As European trading began, the dollar rose broadly. Reuters reported the dollar index up 0.38% at 101.58, the euro down 0.3% at $1.1299, its first fall below $1.13 since May 2025, and US 10-year and 30-year yields at new highs of about 5.34% and 5.67% overnight, after their largest quarterly rise since 1994. None of the sources read names a single piece of news behind the move at the open.
happened.why: Higher US yields make dollars more rewarding to hold, so money moves into the dollar and each pound buys fewer dirhams.
happened.effect: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3263 at 11:10 Dubai to a low near 1.3226 at 11:45 Dubai, a drop of about 0.28% in 35 minutes, then steadied near 1.3235.

happened.event: Sterling drifts lower in Asian trading
happened.result: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3271 at 05:10 Dubai to about 1.3252 by 07:40 Dubai. The dollar also firmed against the yen after Japan's business survey, and none of the sources read names a single piece of news behind the move.
happened.why: When the dollar is broadly firmer in thin overnight trading, each pound buys fewer dollars and so fewer dirhams.
happened.effect: A fall of about 0.15% over two and a half hours, taking GBP/AED from about 4.874 to about 4.867.

happened.result: Big manufacturers' confidence came in at +24 against +25 expected, and big service firms at +35 against +36. Bank of Japan meeting notes showed some members open to faster rises, but traders trimmed bets on a rise in October and the dollar rose to about 157.87 yen.
happened.why: A firmer dollar against the yen usually comes with a firmer dollar more generally, which means fewer dirhams per pound.
happened.effect: GBP/USD barely moved at the release, easing from 1.3265 to 1.3262 within five minutes.

happened.event: Fed's Kashkari speaks in New York
happened.result: Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said inflation of about 3% is still too high and the latest data do not change his view. He has pencilled in one more rise this year and another in 2027, and said the longer the economy stays strong, the more he questions whether policy is tight at all.
happened.why: A Fed official leaning towards more rises supports US yields and the dollar, so each pound buys fewer dirhams.
happened.effect: GBP/USD dipped from 1.3263 to 1.3260 at the start of his remarks, in thin trading at the daily rollover, then recovered to about 1.3265 within ten minutes.

happened.event: US-Iran talks stall, while oil eases this morning
happened.result: Secretary of State Rubio ordered Iran's UN delegation to leave New York after indirect talks stalled; Iran says it has received the official US response to its latest peace offer. Oil futures fell this morning on quiet news from the Gulf, with Brent for December down about 1.2% and US crude down about 1.7% in early European trading.
happened.why: Gulf tension keeps a risk premium in oil and supports the dollar as a safe haven, while cheaper oil eases US inflation worries; this morning the two pulled in opposite directions.
happened.effect: No sharp move in GBP/USD is linked to either; the fall in oil did not stop the dollar rising with US yields.

drivers.title: US bond yields
drivers.text: US 10-year and 30-year yields reached new highs overnight, about 5.34% and 5.67% on Reuters' figures, after their largest quarterly rise since 1994. High US yields keep the dollar attractive to hold and are the main weight on sterling today.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: After Wednesday's cooler inflation figures, markets put about a 39% chance on a quarter-point Fed rise at the 28 October meeting, down from about 45% before them, and the CME FedWatch tool shows about an 87% chance of a rise by the end of the year. Fed speakers lean firm: Kashkari and Cook stress that inflation has been too high for too long, while Williams sees no urgency. Friday's jobs report is the next big test.

drivers.title: A broadly stronger dollar
drivers.text: The dollar index stood near 101.6 on Thursday morning, near its mid-May highs, after a sixth quarterly gain in a row. The euro fell nearly 2.5% in September and is below $1.13, so sterling's fall today is part of a wider dollar move rather than news particular to the UK.

drivers.title: Oil and the Middle East
drivers.text: Brent settled at $98.03 (about £74.16) on Wednesday and eased about 1.2% this morning. Gulf exports are close to pre-war levels, but fuel stocks are very low and US-Iran talks have stalled, so oil remains sensitive to news from the Gulf.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 17 September, with three of the nine members voting for a rise, and markets price a quarter-point rise at the 5 November meeting. UK growth in April to June was revised up on Wednesday. At about 1.3219, GBP/AED is near 4.855 at the peg of 3.6725, close to the 12-week low near 1.3200 reached last week.

lower: US weekly jobless claims today below the 201K forecast, or the US factory survey (ISM) above 54.8, which would point to a strong US economy and support the dollar.
US jobs figures on Friday stronger than the 90K forecast, or wages rising faster than 0.3%, which would revive the chance of an October Fed rise and strengthen the dollar.
US 10-year yields rising further from their new highs, which would keep drawing money into the dollar.
Renewed escalation with Iran after the stalled talks, lifting oil again, which tends to strengthen the dollar.
higher: US jobless claims today above the 201K forecast, or the factory survey below 54.8, which would make an October Fed rise less likely and weaken the dollar.
Fed's Waller today sounding patient about further rises, which would lower US yields and weaken the dollar.
US jobs figures on Friday weaker than the 90K forecast, or unemployment above 4.1%, which would make an October Fed rise less likely and weaken the dollar.
Progress in the Qatari mediation with Iran, easing oil, which reduces the demand for dollars.
watch: US weekly jobless claims at 16:30 Dubai today, with 201K forecast; a higher figure would help someone selling pounds for dirhams. Then the US factory survey (ISM) and Fed's Waller, both at 18:00 Dubai, with 54.8 forecast for the survey; a lower reading or a patient tone would help. Friday's US jobs report at 16:30 Dubai, with 90K jobs and 4.1% unemployment forecast, is the week's main event: weaker figures would help, stronger would hurt.
